transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because... I just don't care about anything anymore. I used to do things, but now I have no interest in my art classes, or board-game nights, or hiking. I don't even care about getting back to the soccer team. I really just sit in my room while everything slips away.
Do you feel sad most of the time?
Yeah, I do. Most days I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling right in my chest. It's just... it's always there. It feels like there’s no future for me beyond the apartment walls.
Do you still enjoy things you used to like, or has the pleasure gone away?

Like I said a minute ago, the pleasure is just completely gone. I really don't care about any of it anymore. Um... my art classes, the board-game nights, hiking... even soccer. I used to like them, but now I just don't have it in me to care. I'd really rather just sit in my room and let it all slip by.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Well, it started getting really bad... I mean, constant, around last summer. So I guess it's been about a year and four months now that I've felt like this every day.
Have you had thoughts of hurting yourself or ending your life?

Yeah, I have. I just... I keep having these thoughts that I don't want to wake up anymore. It's just too much. Actually, the other day, my friend came over and found me... I was just sitting there, saying out loud that I couldn't keep living like this. So, yeah, the thoughts are definitely there.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level or how you move throughout the day?

Yeah, it really goes back and forth. Um... some days I just pace. I'll walk from the kitchen to the window, over and over, until my legs actually ache. But then other times, I just move so slowly. Just doing something simple, like trying to make coffee... it feels like lifting wet cement. I just have no energy for it.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight since you started feeling this way?

Yeah, I've lost quite a bit of weight. I usually go most of the day without eating... food just tastes like cardboard to me now, so I don't really want it. It's gotten to the point where my jeans are so loose that I actually have to knot the waistband just to keep them on.
Have you had any periods in the last year where you felt significantly better for at least a couple of months?

No, I haven't. Um... it's just been a constant struggle, honestly. I don't remember the last time I felt okay for more than a day or two, let alone a couple of months. It's just been this... this heavy feeling all year.
Have you had any periods where your symptoms were so severe that you couldn't leave the house or take care of yourself?

Yeah, it's... it's gotten pretty bad. I've completely stopped taking any freelance art-education work. I just can't manage it. And I don't go to community events or play soccer anymore, either. I barely leave the house. Honestly, my friend has been coming over to check on me because... well, I'm just not reliably eating or showering. She makes sure I'm actually keeping myself safe, because left to my own devices, I just... I don't do those things right now.
Have you ever had a period where your symptoms were less severe, but still noticeable, and you were able to manage your daily life with some effort?

Yeah, there was a stretch before the worst of this depression set in. I was able to manage a bit better then. I could still cook for myself sometimes, and I'd reply to my friends when they checked in. But... even then, things weren't right. For a few weeks during that time, I was already hearing the voice. And I was convinced that the flickering lights in the hallway were sending signals specifically about me. So I was functioning a little, but I was still dealing with all of that.
You mentioned hearing a voice and thinking the flickering lights were sending signals about you, are you still experiencing those kinds of thoughts or perceptions?

Yeah, I am. They haven't really stopped. Um... the voices and those beliefs about being watched, they actually started a few months after my divorce. So I guess it's been going on for about a year and eight months now.
Are the voices you hear still commenting on your thoughts or actions?

Yeah, she does. Um... it's a woman's voice. I usually hear it coming from the corner of my room. She tells me that I ruined everything and that I should just stay inside. It's not just a thought, though... it sounds as clear as if someone was standing right next to my bed talking to me.
Do you ever find it hard to express your thoughts or feel like your thoughts are disjointed or don't make sense to others?

Yes, that happens a lot. When I try to explain what's been happening, my thoughts just... they jump around. I'll start talking about the divorce papers, and then suddenly I'm thinking about paint colors, and then the number seven. People keep telling me they can't follow what I'm saying, that it doesn't make sense to them.
Are the voices or the feelings of being watched and receiving signals dominating your thoughts most of the time?

Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't really noticed if they dominate my thoughts most of the time. I know the voice and the signals are there, but I couldn't really tell you if they take up the majority of my day or not. I just haven't kept track of it like that.
Have you ever experienced the voices or feelings of being watched when you weren't feeling depressed?

Yes. Um... there was a stretch before the worst of the depression set in. I was still able to cook sometimes, and I was actually answering my friends when they called. But even then, I was already hearing the woman's voice. And I had been believing that the hallway lights were sending signals about me for weeks at that point. So, yeah, it was happening before I felt this low.
Do the voices and feelings of being watched only happen when you're feeling really down, or do they also occur when your mood is not as low?

I think I just mentioned this, but yes, they happen even when I'm not feeling as low. Like I said, there was a time before the worst of the depression hit. I was still managing to cook a little bit, and I was answering the phone when my friends called. But even during that time, I was already hearing the woman's voice. And I had been thinking the hallway lights were sending signals about me for weeks before the depression got really bad. So they definitely happen when my mood isn't as low.
Are the things the voice says to you usually about how bad you feel or how hopeless you are?

Yeah, it usually is about that kind of stuff. I hear a woman's voice coming from the corner of my room, and she tells me that I ruined everything. She says I should just stay inside. It's not like a thought in my head, either... it sounds as clear as if someone was standing right next to my bed talking to me.
Are the things the voice says to you usually consistent with your feelings of sadness and hopelessness?

Yeah, they definitely line up. Like I was just saying, she tells me I ruined everything. Um... for much of this past year, the really low mood and the voices have just been happening at the exact same time. I'll be lying in bed, feeling completely hopeless, and right while I'm feeling that way, I'm also hearing that woman telling me how I ruined it all. So, yeah, it's very consistent.
Are the voices and the things they say to you always related to your feelings of sadness and hopelessness?

I feel like I just answered this, but... yeah. I don't know if it's every single time, but mostly, yes. Like I just said, she usually just tells me I ruined everything. I haven't really noticed her saying anything that isn't about that kind of stuff.
